summary: Iteration 12 targeted re-verification of the Metro web-bundle fix (platform-specific wrapper files under /app/frontend/src/native/). VERDICT: FIX CONFIRMED. (1) curl http://localhost:3000/node_modules/expo-router/entry.bundle?platform=web now returns HTTP 200 (8.6 MB, 1544 modules, was 500). Metro logs are clean — 'Web Bundled 7713ms ... (1544 modules)' with no resolveAssetSource errors. (2) Backend regression: 22/22 pytest PASS in 2.57s (test_kizilkan_api.py — Health, M3U, Xtream, Stalker, EPG, DVR). (3) Frontend interactive smoke on http://localhost:3000 (mobile viewport 390x844): home splash renders KIZILKAN Player with 'Oynatma Listesi Ekle' CTA; /downloads renders empty state 'Henüz indirme yok' with cloud-download-outline icon and helper text; settings screen shows İndirilenler row and tapping feature-downloads-btn navigates to /downloads (URL confirmed as http://localhost:3000/downloads). No pageerrors, no red screen, no crash. All 4 new wrapper files (vlc.native.ts, vlc.web.ts, cast.native.ts, cast.web.ts) correctly structured — web variants export null, native variants use try/require. Only benign RN-Web deprecation warnings observed (textShadow*/shadow*/pointerEvents style props, expo-notifications push token on web, useNativeDriver falling back to JS) — none are blockers.
critical_code_review_comments: Wrapper pattern is correct: vlc.native.ts / cast.native.ts use try/require guarded so a missing native module returns null instead of throwing at import; vlc.web.ts / cast.web.ts export null. Metro's platform resolver picks the right file — VLC and google-cast never enter the web bundle, resolving the previous 'Missing ./build/resolveAssetSource specifier' failure at its root.

Non-blocking RN-Web warnings surfaced during smoke: textShadow*/shadow* style props deprecated, props.pointerEvents deprecated, useNativeDriver missing RCTAnimation (JS fallback). These are cosmetic on web preview and should be tracked as follow-up cleanup, not this iteration's scope.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (3/3 smoke tests: home render, /downloads empty state, settings→downloads navigation)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Web bundle blocker is resolved; app is fully loadable on http://localhost:3000. Future iterations can safely exercise UI flows for Faz B.1 (VLC dual-engine), B.2 (Chromecast), B.4 (Downloads) — with the caveat that VLC playback and the Cast picker cannot be exercised in the web preview (they render as null there). Any deeper native-only behavior must be tested via Expo Go / native build. Deprecation warnings for textShadow*/shadow*/pointerEvents can be cleaned up but are non-blocking.
rca_of_issue: Previous iteration_11 RCA: static require() inside Platform.OS guard was traversed by Metro, pulling react-native-vlc-media-player → react-native/Libraries/Image/resolveAssetSource → expo-asset which broke web bundling (500). Fix (verified): platform-suffixed modules under /app/frontend/src/native/. Metro's resolver picks *.web.ts for web (returns null) and *.native.ts for iOS/Android, so the native-only dependency is excluded from the web bundle entirely. Bundle now returns 200; app renders; empty-state downloads route works; settings→downloads navigation works.
